description: Actual POLIS V4 synthetic demonstration; not empirical observations

protocol.initialCondition: Fresh generated society for each seed; preferences, topology and future randomness vary.
protocol.parameterAssumptions: Independent user-specified distributions, sampled once per simulation; equal run weights. They are assumptions, not a learned posterior.
protocol.probabilityTarget: Winner at the final simulated round, with none as a fourth outcome.
protocol.metricTarget: Arithmetic mean over final 20 simulated rounds.
protocol.shareDefinition: Share of counted plurality votes among participating agents.
protocol.validationStatus: Scenario ensemble only. No empirical calibration or forecasting accuracy has been established.

warnings: All probabilities and quantiles are conditional on this model, settings and user parameter distributions. They are not election forecasts with validated coverage.
Monte Carlo SE measures finite independent-run simulation error, not misspecification, observation error, empirical uncertainty or omitted political mechanisms.
Represented population only scales illustrative counts uniformly. It does not add simulated agents, census weighting, sampling validity or precision.
A high win probability is not welfare optimality, fairness, equilibrium or MARL convergence.
Parameter variation and stochastic/population variation are mixed in this ensemble; no formal variance decomposition or Bayesian posterior is claimed.

sources.title: Forecasting elections with agent-based modeling: Two live experiments

sources.access: Full article introduction, platform/model-screening methodology and results/discussion reviewed.
sources.use: Motivates fitting against aggregate histories and separately checking forecasts. POLIS does not reproduce their demographic models or import their empirical effect sizes.

sources.access: Abstract and sections 2, 3.1–3.2, including calibration criteria and surrogate-validation distinctions reviewed.
sources.use: Motivates a bounded calibration budget and checking original simulation outputs. This module evaluates the actual engine directly; it does not implement the paper’s XGBoost active-learning surrogate.

sources.title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
sources.access: Introduction, section 3 categorical scoring rules and section 6 interval discussion reviewed.
sources.use: Informs multiclass Brier/logarithmic losses and the separation of probabilistic sharpness from calibration. Simulation quantiles are not advertised as empirically calibrated prediction intervals.

observations.label: Synthetic demonstration generated by POLIS; not observed people

protocol.selection: Minimum equally weighted MSE across observed numeric aggregate fields and training rounds only. Candidate order breaks exact ties.
protocol.validation: Later observation rounds and disjoint simulation seeds; holdout labels never select parameters.

trainingScores.scoring: Multiclass loss over A/B/C/none; winner probabilities receive a symmetric one-count pseudocount (n+4 denominator). Numeric fields/rounds equally weighted. Lower losses are better. Coverage is descriptive across supplied fields/rounds, not a coverage guarantee.

holdoutScores.scoring: Multiclass loss over A/B/C/none; winner probabilities receive a symmetric one-count pseudocount (n+4 denominator). Numeric fields/rounds equally weighted. Lower losses are better. Coverage is descriptive across supplied fields/rounds, not a coverage guarantee.

baseline.method: Numeric persistence: last available training observation per field. Winner probability: Laplace-smoothed training winner frequencies. No holdout labels enter the baseline.

scores.scoring: Multiclass loss over A/B/C/none; winner probabilities receive a symmetric one-count pseudocount (n+4 denominator). Numeric fields/rounds equally weighted. Lower losses are better. Coverage is descriptive across supplied fields/rounds, not a coverage guarantee.

calibration.status: Synthetic recovery/validation exercise; no empirical forecasting evidence.
warnings: Held-out observations are not used to select parameters. Repeatedly changing settings after inspecting this holdout turns it into development data; obtain a new untouched evaluation set.
A good aggregate fit does not identify the true behavioral mechanism. Multiple parameter combinations can fit the same history.
This is direct bounded engine-grid calibration, not XGBoost, Bayesian inference, a causal estimator or a demographic forecasting system.
Adjacent observation rounds may be dependent. Descriptive errors and interval coverage do not establish calibration on future independent elections.
Approval/Borda shares are normalized counted rule scores. Only matching rule/score observations are accepted.
No individual voter records, real targeting policy or empirical parameter defaults are imported.
